ideas.description: Move the block-1 freeze earlier, from 0.8 to 0.7 of training samples. The tip is E058 (commit fb3f626): bs 1536; 20 px for epochs 0-1.5 and 28 px for 1.5-3.5, both without translate; 32 px with translate-2 for 3.5-6.75; jitter in every stage; SGD-group lr x1.5; head lr x2 with wd halved; Muon lr 0.16, mom 0.8, NS3; lookahead 0.97^5; whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only; block 1 frozen from 5.4 epochs. If I077 or I078 is kept first, use that successor. Make one change: switch to the existing block-1-frozen graph pair 0.675 epoch earlier, at sample 236250 (4.725 epochs) instead of 270000. That pair is the 32 px train step with block 1's output detached, plus the Muon variant without the 128x1152 group, with block-1 BN biases skipped in the SGD group. Block 1 still runs forward in train mode, so its BN running stats keep updating, and lookahead keeps blending it. Total epochs, stage boundaries, bs, the sample stream and every schedule stay unchanged. The switch falls inside step ~153, so split that straddling step into the two partial shapes, as the existing switches do. In build(), warm up both new partial shapes (unfrozen and frozen 32 px graphs) with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py on the new shapes and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times. Rationale: E058 priced the last 20% at ~0.02 pp per 1% of time, the cheapest lever found so far (D025 C0237/C0246: early layers converge first). This run prices the next 10%.
ideas.expected: Time -1.5% to -3.5%, point -2.4% (~4.58 s vs 4.696 s): 0.675 more epochs at the block-1-frozen cost (~0.65 vs ~0.82 s/epoch at 32 px). Accuracy 0.7505-0.7555, point 0.7532 (-0.05 pp; this 10% lies at a higher lr than the last 20%, so it should cost a bit more per sample than E058 did). Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep, new best; then price 0.6. Infeasible by <=0.1 pp: keep the code path and pair it with +0.25 epoch (the combine idea). Drop >=0.3 pp: the block-1 freeze is at its floor near 0.8; close earlier-freeze tuning.

ideas.description: FreezeOut cascade: freeze block 2 for the last 10% of samples, following D025 (b) and C0239. Block 2 is frozen only after block 1, because in a skip-free net detaching block 2 cuts all gradient to block 1. On the tip (E058, or the successor of the block-1-at-0.7 idea, I077 or I078 if one is kept), make one change: from sample 303750 (6.075 epochs, 0.9 of samples) to the end, use a fourth 32 px train-step graph variant in which block 2's output is detached. Blocks 1 and 2 still run forward in train mode, so their BN running stats keep updating. Pair it with a third compiled Muon-step variant that contains only the 576-wide block-3 shape group, and skip block-1 and block-2 BN biases in the SGD group through the same variant flag. The backward then skips block 2's wgrad and dgrad and block 3's first-conv dgrad. Conv FLOPs per step fall from ~0.81x to ~0.49x of an unfrozen 32 px step. Lookahead still blends blocks 1 and 2. Pick the variant in Python by sample count, with no data-dependent branch in the graph. Split the straddling step at 303750 into the two partial shapes. In build(), warm up the new train and Muon variants plus every partial shape at the 0.9 switch and at the run end, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Keep build under ~450 s. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.
ideas.expected: Time -2.5% to -5.5%, point -3.9% (~4.51 s): 0.675 epoch drops from ~0.65 to ~0.38 s/epoch, plus the 384-group NS/projection on those steps. Accuracy 0.749-0.755, point 0.7522 (-0.15 pp). Block 2 is the largest block, and late layers converge later than block 1 (C0237), so this should cost more per sample than E058. Likely infeasible alone at the 0.07 pp margin. Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep, new best. Infeasible by <=0.15 pp with time down >=3%: keep the code path and pair it with +0.25 epoch. Drop >=0.35 pp: late block-2 learning matters; close the cascade at block 1 and refute H2.4.7's extension to block 2.

ideas.description: Cash in the freeze exchange rate as margin. Freezing costs ~0.02-0.05 pp per 1% of time, while 32 px epochs buy ~0.08-0.15 pp per 1%, so freeze-more plus more epochs should net time at equal accuracy. Run this only after the block-1-at-0.7 and block-2-cascade ideas have been read. Base: the faster feasible commit among them if one was kept. Otherwise stack every freeze change that was infeasible by <=0.15 pp onto E058; if neither qualifies, skip this idea. Make one change: total epochs 6.75 -> 7.0, with the extra 0.25 epoch added to the 32 px stage (stage boundaries at 1.5 and 3.5 epochs stay in samples). Scale the lr warmup and decay, the Muon multiplier and the lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp to samples seen. Keep the freeze points as fractions of total samples (for example 0.7 and 0.9), so they move proportionally. The last quarter-epoch uses the first quarter of that epoch's permutation, as in E027. In build(), warm up every new partial shape at the moved freeze switches and at the new run end for each graph variant, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py on new shapes and compare trial-0 with later-trial times.
ideas.expected: If both freeze cuts are stacked (block 1 from 0.7, block 2 from 0.9): 32 px time ~2.32 s against the tip's ~2.44 s, so total time ~4.58 s (-2.4%, range -1% to -4%). Accuracy 0.751-0.758, point 0.7545: the stack costs ~-0.2 pp and +0.25 epoch adds ~+0.25-0.3 pp. Feasible and >=1% faster than the then-tip: keep, new best with ~0.15 pp margin, and continue the freeze-more-plus-epochs ladder (block 1 at 0.6). If it is feasible but not faster, the freeze cost per sample is rising faster than estimated; stop the ladder.

ideas.description: Partial freezing by update thinning, as an explore against a hard earlier freeze. On the tip (E058 or its successor), make one change: during the 32 px stage before the existing freeze (samples 175000-270000, epochs 3.5-5.4), run the existing block-1-frozen graph pair (detached block-1 output, and the Muon variant without the 128x1152 group) on every odd step, and the normal graph pair on even steps. On frozen steps block 1 gets no gradient: its Muon momentum buffer is not updated and its BN biases are skipped in SGD, while its BN running stats still update. The lr schedules are unchanged, so block 1 takes half as many rotations in that window, each from a full-batch gradient. Pick the variant in Python by step parity, with no data-dependent branch. No new graphs are needed, since both variants already exist at 32 px. Warm up any new partial shape at the 3.5-epoch and 5.4-epoch switches with both variants in the exact timed layout (E035). Compare trial-0 with later-trial times.
ideas.expected: Time -2.5% to -4.5%, point -3.4% (~4.54 s): about half of 1.9 epochs moves to the frozen cost (~0.17 s/epoch saved on half the steps). Accuracy 0.749-0.755, point 0.7525 (-0.12 pp). Grading against the block-1-at-0.7 idea, which saves ~2.4%: if thinning costs less accuracy per 1% of time than the hard earlier freeze, block 1 needs recency of updates rather than update count; then stack thinning over 0.3-0.8 with the 0.8 freeze. A drop >=0.3 pp means block-1 updates at peak or mid lr carry real value per step; then only tail freezing is cheap. Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep.

ideas.description: RMS-matched test of scheduled orthogonalization strength. This is the form requested when I054 was dropped, so that a result is not confounded with a lower effective Muon lr (H1.2.4). On the tip (E058 or its successor), make one change inside the batched compiled Muon step. Today each momentum matrix is scaled to Frobenius norm 1 before NS3. Instead, scale it to s_t, which decays linearly from 0.50 at step 0 to 0.08 at the final step (Hiverge's CIFAR-10 schedule). Run the same 3 quintic iterations, then rescale each NS output matrix so its Frobenius norm equals that of the tip's NS output for that shape group (or, more simply, sqrt(min(out,in)) times the existing sqrt(max(1,out/in)) factor). The per-step update magnitude is therefore unchanged, and only how strongly the small singular directions are flattened changes. Pass s_t as a 0-d GPU tensor updated with fill_, so nothing recompiles. Weight-norm projection, Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead, the curriculum, freeze points and epochs stay unchanged. In drafts/, log the per-group update Frobenius norm and the fraction of singular values above 0.5 at steps 0, 100 and the end, against the tip, to confirm the norms match and the spectrum is less whitened late in training. Run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and re-warm the Muon variants in build().
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.35 to +0.30 pp, point 0.0 pp (~0.7537). Time +0% to +0.5% (one extra norm and scale per group). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.9: late, less-whitened updates help at fixed magnitude, which banks margin for the freeze ladder. Within +-0.15 pp: orthogonalization strength is not a lever at this horizon; close H1.9 and drop H1.9.1. A drop >=0.3 pp means full whitening throughout is right, consistent with E030's lesson that equalizing directions the gradient barely asked for can hurt.

ideas.description: NorMuon on the conv filters. On the tip (E058 or its successor), make one change inside the batched compiled Muon step: after NS3 and before the sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling, apply per-row (per output filter) second-moment normalization. Keep a buffer v per group of shape [n_mats, out, 1], initialised to zero in prepare() (reset per trial). Update v = 0.95*v + 0.05*mean_over_cols(O^2) and set O' = O / sqrt(v_hat + 1e-8), with bias correction v_hat = v / (1 - 0.95^t). Then rescale O' to the Frobenius norm O had, so the per-step update magnitude is unchanged and only its distribution across filters changes. The weight-norm projection, Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead, curriculum, freeze variants and epochs stay unchanged. The frozen-block Muon variants must update v only for the groups they contain. Pass the step count as a 0-d tensor. Re-warm all Muon variants in build() on synthetic tensors, and run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.30 to +0.35 pp, point +0.05 pp. Paired with per-filter weight-norm projection, equal per-filter update RMS gives every filter a more even relative rotation. NorMuon is untested on CNN filters. Time +0.2% to +1.0%, point +0.5% (one memory-bound pass over ~11M params per step). A gain >=0.25 pp supports H1.2.6 and banks margin for the freeze ladder. Within +-0.15 pp: Muon's update geometry is saturated on the filters; close H1.2.6. A drop >=0.25 pp refutes it.

That is roughly 4-7x cheaper than adding epochs (about 0.08-0.15 pp per 1%) and the cheapest lever found so far. So the queue is built around a freeze ladder.

**New ideas, in run order:**
1. **Block-1 freeze at 0.7 (priority 5).** Freeze block 1 from 0.7 of samples instead of 0.8. Expected: -2.4% time, about -0.05 pp, so roughly 0.7532, right at the gate.
2. **Block-2 freeze at 0.9 (priority 4).** Also freeze block 2 for the last 10%. A step with both blocks frozen costs about half an unfrozen one. Expected: -3.9% time, about -0.15 pp, which probably misses the gate on its own.
3. **Combine with +0.25 epoch (priority 3, conditional).** Once ideas 1 and 2 are read, stack the kept or near-miss freeze cuts and add 0.25 epoch to the 32 px stage. This turns the cheap freeze cost into extra margin. Expected: about -2.4% time, about 0.7545.

**Exploration:**
- **Update thinning (priority 2, H2.4.7).** Update block 1 only on alternate steps between 3.5 and 5.4 epochs. This tells us whether block 1 needs recent updates or many updates.
- **Weaker late orthogonalization at fixed update size (priority 2, H1.9).** Muon whitens the update less strongly late in training (a Frobenius-norm schedule before the 3 Newton-Schulz steps), with the update size matched to the tip's. This removes the lower-effective-lr confound that got I054 dropped.
- **NorMuon (priority 1, H1.2.6).** Per-filter normalization after the 3 Newton-Schulz steps, with the update size kept the same.

**Queue status:**
- I078 (whitening bias trained through the 28 px stage) stays queued. H6.1.1 is still open and the idea applies to the new tip.
- I077 (Muon on the head) is still running.
- Nothing was dropped: no queued idea's hypothesis has been settled.

That leaves 7 queued ideas. Because the margin is so thin, each new idea says to keep its code for pairing when it misses the gate by 0.1-0.15 pp or less.
